EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT & HOSPITAL ADMISSION NOTE
Encounter Date: October 05, 2026 (Time: 21:30 EDT)
Patient: Robert Morales (DOB: 02/14/1965, Age: 61, Male)
Attending Physician: Dr. Jason Miller, MD

PRESENTATION:
Patient presented to the emergency department with intermittent non-radiating retrosternal chest pressure starting 3 hours prior to arrival while watching television. He endorses mild shortness of breath, denied diaphoresis, syncope, or radiating jaw/arm pain.

INITIAL CLINICAL ASSESSMENT & VITALS:
- Blood Pressure: 134/78 mmHg
- Heart Rate: 72 bpm, regular rhythm
- Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths/min
- Oxygen Saturation: 98% on room air
- Physical Exam: Well appearing, alert, oriented x 4. Lungs clear to auscultation bilaterally. Heart sounds S1/S2 present, no murmurs, rubs, or gallops. No peripheral edema, no signs of hypoperfusion.

DIAGNOSTIC WORKUP:
- 12-Lead ECG (21:45): Normal sinus rhythm at 70 bpm, normal axis, no acute ST-segment elevation or depression, no T-wave inversions.
- High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin I (0 hours): 4.1 ng/L (Normal reference < 14 ng/L).
- High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin I (3 hours): 4.3 ng/L (Delta flat, non-elevated).
- Repeat ECG at 3 hours: Unchanged, no acute ischemic abnormalities.

HOSPITAL COURSE & LENGTH OF STAY:
Patient was admitted under inpatient status at 01:15 on Oct 06. He remained pain-free overnight on aspirin and telemetry. A pharmacological nuclear stress test was performed at 14:00 on Oct 06, which demonstrated normal myocardial perfusion with an ejection fraction of 62% and no reversible ischemia. Serial troponin at 12 hours remained negative (4.0 ng/L). Patient was discharged home in stable condition at 19:30 on Oct 06 (Total length of stay: 22 hours across 0 midnights).

UTILIZATION REVIEW QUESTION:
Does patient meet medical necessity criteria for Acute Inpatient Admission under CMS Two-Midnight Rule, or should status be reclassified as Outpatient Observation?
